examples.en: My mother interferes too much in my affairs.
Don't meddle in other people's private lives.
My boss interfered even in small things.
I get stressed because of a friend who meddles.

examples.ko: 아이를 믿고 너무 간섭하기보다 지켜보기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to trust my child and watch rather than interfere too much.

examples.ko: 한 나라가 다른 나라의 일에 간섭하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: One country must not interfere in another country's affairs.

explain: 간섭하다는 남의 일에 필요 이상으로 끼어들어 이래라저래라 하는 거예요. '도와주다'와 달리 듣는 사람이 불편하다고 느끼는 뜻이 들어 있어요. '~에 간섭하다'처럼 '에'와 써요.

phrases.example: 부모님이 제 친구 문제에 간섭을 해요.
phrases.en: My parents interfere in my friend problems.
phrases.nuance_ko: '간섭하다'를 '간섭을 하다'로 풀어서 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A spread-out form of 간섭하다.

phrases.example: 저는 일할 때 간섭을 받는 게 싫어요.
phrases.en: I don't like being interfered with when I work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람이 끼어드는 일을 겪는 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the side of the person being interfered with.

phrases.en: I don't want to meddle in my friend's business.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남의 일에 끼어들지 않겠다는 마음을 부드럽게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Softly says you don't want to step into someone else's matters.

explain_en: 간섭하다 is to step into someone else's business more than needed and tell them what to do. Unlike '도와주다' (to help), it carries a sense that the other person finds it unwelcome. It takes 에: '~에 간섭하다'.

examples.en: I quickly pulled the fighting kids apart.
The war tore the family apart.
Please split the cake in half.
Someone is trying to come between us.
A river divides the village into two.
A money problem drove the two friends apart.

explain: 붙어 있거나 가까운 것을 둘로 나누어 떨어뜨린다는 뜻이에요. 물건을 나눌 때뿐 아니라 사람 사이를 멀어지게 할 때도 써요. 사람 관계에서는 '사이를 갈라놓다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: Who drove those two people apart?
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 관계를 멀어지게 한다는 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural pairing for driving a wedge between people.

phrases.en: Please don't separate the two friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 하지 말라고 부탁하는 존댓말 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite form used to ask someone not to do it.

phrases.en: To stop the fight, I separated the two and talked to them.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고'로 이어서 떼어 놓은 다음 하는 일을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: -고 links what you do after pulling them apart.

explain_en: It means separating things that were joined or close into two parts. It works for dividing objects and also for driving people apart. For relationships, '사이를 갈라놓다' is the natural phrase.

examples.ko: 이 일은 경험자만 지원할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Only experienced people can apply for this job.
Hearing from someone with experience helped me.
I feel at ease when an experienced person is beside me.
Our shop hires experienced people first.

examples.ko: 그는 이 분야의 경험자라서 설명을 잘해요.
examples.en: He is experienced in this field, so he explains well.
An experienced person and a beginner were put in the same group.

explain: 구인 공고의 '경험자 우대'라는 말로 많이 봐요. 반대말은 '초보자'나 '미경험자'예요. 일 이야기에서는 '경력자'를 더 자주 써요. '경험자'는 일뿐 아니라 여행, 시험 같은 일상 경험에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The job posting says 'experienced people preferred'.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구인 공고에서 가장 많이 보는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The expression you see most often in job postings.

phrases.en: This shop is looking for someone with work experience.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일 이야기에서는 '경력자'가 더 자주 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: In talk about work, 경력자 is used more often.

phrases.en: Before the trip, I asked someone who had been there.
phrases.nuance_ko: 먼저 해 본 사람에게 조언을 구할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking advice from someone who has done it.

explain_en: You often see '경험자 우대' in job ads. Its opposites are '초보자' and '미경험자'. For work, '경력자' is more common. '경험자' also works for everyday experiences like travel or exams.

examples.ko: 공인은 말과 행동에 더 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: Public figures have to be more careful with their words and actions.

examples.ko: 유명한 가수는 공인이라서 사생활이 자주 알려져요.
examples.en: A famous singer is a public figure, so their private life often becomes known.

examples.ko: 정치인이나 연예인 같은 공인에게는 큰 책임이 있어요.
examples.en: Public figures like politicians and entertainers carry great responsibility.
As a public figure, he posted an apology.

examples.ko: 공인의 말은 많은 사람에게 영향을 줘요.
examples.en: A public figure's words influence many people.

examples.ko: 저는 공인이 아니니까 평범하게 살고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'm not a public figure, so I want to live an ordinary life.

explain: 정치인, 연예인, 공무원처럼 많은 사람이 지켜보는 사람에게 써요. '공인이라서 조심해야 한다'는 말을 자주 해요. '공인 중개사'의 공인은 공식 인정이라는 다른 말이라 헷갈리기 쉬워요.

phrases.en: That actor is a public figure, so he is careful about his behavior.
phrases.nuance_ko: '공인'과 가장 자주 함께 나오는 이유 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common way to give a reason with this word.

phrases.en: As a public figure, you have to be careful with your words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공인의 입장이나 책임을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the role or responsibility of a public figure.

phrases.en: A public figure's words come with great responsibility.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '의'를 붙여 공인에게 요구되는 점을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 의 lets you talk about what is expected of a public figure.

explain_en: It is used for people many others watch, such as politicians, entertainers and civil servants, as in '공인이라서 조심해야 한다' (as a public figure, one must be careful). The 공인 in '공인 중개사' (licensed real estate agent) is a different word meaning officially recognized, so it is easy to mix up.

examples.en: My throat felt scratchy, so I drank some water.
For some reason things are awkward between that person and me.
Let's talk about the awkward stuff later.
I have a cold and my throat is scratchy.
Since our fight, it's awkward to meet my friend.

examples.ko: 이 천은 만지면 껄끄러운 느낌이 나요.
examples.en: This fabric feels scratchy to the touch.

explain: 촉감이 거칠다는 뜻도 있지만, 사람 사이가 어색하고 불편할 때도 많이 써요. '불편하다'보다 은근히 어색하고 마주하기 부담스러운 느낌이에요. 'ㅂ' 불규칙이라서 '껄끄러워요', '껄끄러운'으로 바뀌어요.

phrases.example: 싸운 뒤로 그 친구와 껄끄러운 사이가 됐어요.
phrases.en: Since the fight, that friend and I have become awkward with each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 사이가 어색하고 불편할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for an awkward, uncomfortable relationship.

phrases.example: 그 사람 앞에서는 말하기가 좀 껄끄러워요.
phrases.en: It feels a bit awkward to speak in front of that person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 활용형으로, 마주하기 부담스러운 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form, used to say that facing someone feels uncomfortable.

phrases.example: 이제는 그 친구를 만나도 껄끄럽지 않아요.
phrases.en: Now I don't feel awkward even when I meet that friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어색함이 사라졌을 때 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when the awkwardness is gone.

explain_en: It can describe a rough, scratchy feel, and it is also often used when a relationship is awkward. Compared with '불편하다', it suggests a subtle awkwardness that makes facing someone burdensome. It is a ㅂ-irregular adjective, so it becomes '껄끄러워요' and '껄끄러운'.

examples.ko: 부모님이 막내를 너무 떠받들어서 버릇이 없어요.
examples.en: His parents dote on the youngest so much that he's spoiled.
He is a person people around him idolize like a hero.
People hailed him as a genius.
It was an era when people revered the king like heaven.

examples.ko: 아이를 떠받들며 키우면 이기적으로 자랄 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you raise a child by pampering him, he can grow up selfish.
Don't just look up to your superiors; look after your colleagues too.

explain: 누군가를 매우 높이고 귀하게 대하는 것이에요. 존경할 때도 쓰지만 지나치게 모시거나 오냐오냐하며 키운다는 부정적인 느낌으로도 자주 써요. 모양이 비슷한 '떠받치다'는 물건이나 구조를 아래서 버티는 말이라 뜻이 달라요.

phrases.en: They raised their only daughter doting on her.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이를 지나치게 귀하게 대하며 키운다는 뜻으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often means raising a child with excessive indulgence.

phrases.en: He is treated like a king on the team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남들이 높이 모신다는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A passive form meaning others hold someone in very high regard.
phrases.en_equiv: to be put on a pedestal

phrases.example: 아이를 너무 떠받들지 말고 가르쳐 주세요.
phrases.en: Please don't spoil the child too much; teach them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 '오냐오냐하지 않다'는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: In the negative, it means not to indulge someone.

explain_en: It means treating someone with great respect and preciousness. It can express admiration, but it is also often used negatively for excessive deference or pampering. The look-alike '떠받치다' means holding something up from below, so the meaning is different.

examples.en: The magician pulled a rabbit out of a hat.
My dream as a child was to be a magician.

examples.ko: 마술사의 손놀림을 눈으로 따라갈 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't follow the magician's hands with my eyes.
We invited a magician to the birthday party.
That magician is good at card tricks.
I clapped for the street magician.

explain: 마술사는 손재주와 기술로 신기한 장면을 보여 주고, 판타지의 '마법사'는 진짜 마법을 써요. 그래서 마술은 무대에서 보고 마법은 이야기 속에서 만나요.

phrases.en: The magician showed the children a magic trick.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마술사가 하는 일을 가장 쉽게 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The simplest common phrase for what a magician does.

phrases.en: I want to become a magician when I grow up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꿈이나 직업을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about dreams or jobs.

phrases.en: I watched a magic show with my family on the weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마술사가 무대에서 하는 공연을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a performance a magician gives on stage.

explain_en: A 마술사 shows amazing tricks with skill and sleight of hand, while a fantasy 마법사 uses real magic. So you see 마술 on stage and meet 마법 in stories.

en: to be harsh; to be cold-hearted; to be heartless

examples.en: You didn't have to turn me down so coldly.
His answer was much colder than I expected.
The boss is so cold that the employees have a hard time.

examples.ko: 매몰찬 현실 앞에서 꿈을 접는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people give up on their dreams in the face of a harsh reality.

examples.ko: 옛 연인이 매몰차다고 느껴서 연락을 끊었어요.
examples.en: I felt my ex was cold-hearted, so I cut off contact.

examples.ko: 매몰차기만 한 사람은 아니에요, 속은 따뜻해요.
examples.en: He's not only cold-hearted; he's warm on the inside.

explain: 인정이나 따뜻함이 없이 쌀쌀맞고 냉정할 때 써요. 말투, 거절, 태도에 자주 쓰고, '냉정하다'보다 상대가 상처받을 만큼 차갑다는 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '매몰차게 거절하다/내치다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: He turned down the request coldly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말로, 인정 없이 단호하게 거절한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation, meaning to refuse harshly without sympathy.

phrases.example: 그 사람의 매몰찬 말투에 상처를 받았어요.
phrases.en: I was hurt by that person's harsh way of speaking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸미는 형태로 말이 차갑고 쌀쌀맞다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for cold, curt speech.

phrases.example: 겉은 차가워 보여도 속은 매몰차지 않은 사람이에요.
phrases.en: Although he looks cold outside, he isn't heartless inside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 그렇게까지 냉정하지는 않다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative form saying someone isn't that cold-hearted.

explain_en: It is used when someone is cold and unfeeling, lacking warmth or compassion. It often goes with tone, refusals, and attitude, and feels colder than '냉정하다', to the point of hurting the other person. It is usually used as '매몰차게 거절하다/내치다'.

examples.en: During vacation, I hang out with my friends in a group.
On the field trip day, the classes ran around in big groups on the playground.
As soon as exams end, students roam downtown in groups.
Shop owners don't like it when kids move around in a pack.
Don't just run around in groups every weekend; study too.
It's a street where tourists move around in crowds, so it's chaotic.

explain: 여러 사람이 무리를 지어 함께 돌아다닐 때 써요. 시끌벅적하고 조금 부정적인 느낌이 들 때가 많아요. 혼자서도 쓸 수 있는 '돌아다니다'와 달리 여럿이 함께일 때만 써요.

phrases.en: The kids go around in a group.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몰려다니다'와 비슷하지만 무리라는 뜻이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 몰려다니다 but makes the idea of a pack clearer.

phrases.en: The hallway is noisy because of the kids running around in groups.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 꾸며 주는 모양이라 조금 부정적으로 들릴 때가 많아요.
phrases.nuance_en: As a describing phrase, it often sounds slightly negative.
phrases.en_equiv: kids who go around in groups

phrases.en: Please don't run around in groups in the hallway.
phrases.nuance_ko: 규칙을 알리거나 주의를 줄 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for rules or warnings.

explain_en: Use it when many people move around together in a group. It often feels noisy and a little negative. Unlike '돌아다니다', which you can do alone, this only works when several people are together.

examples.ko: 그 아이를 문제아라고 부르면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You should not call that child a troublemaker.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 저는 선생님 속을 썩이는 문제아였어요.
examples.en: As a kid I was a troublemaker who worried my teachers.

examples.ko: 영화에는 문제아가 선생님을 만나 달라지는 이야기가 나와요.
examples.en: The movie tells of a troublemaker who changes after meeting a teacher.
I heard he had a hard time after being labeled a troublemaker at school.
A counseling program for problem kids has been created.
He changed from a troublemaker to a model student.

explain: 행동 때문에 학교나 집에서 걱정을 끼치는 아이를 말해요. 듣는 아이에게는 상처가 될 수 있어서 직접 앞에서 부르는 말로는 잘 안 써요. 반대말로는 '모범생'을 많이 써요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling was a troublemaker as a child.
phrases.nuance_ko: '문제아'보다 가볍고 귀엽게 말하는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lighter and more affectionate than 문제아.

phrases.en: That friend is the model student in our class.
phrases.nuance_ko: '문제아'의 반대말로, 행동과 공부가 모두 바른 학생이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 문제아: a well-behaved, diligent student.

phrases.en: Please don't treat the child like a troublemaker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제아가 아닌데 그렇게 대할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone is treated like a troublemaker unfairly.

explain_en: It refers to a child whose behavior worries school or family. It can hurt the child, so it is rarely used to someone's face. Its common opposite is 모범생.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 우리 반에서 별종으로 통해요.
examples.en: That friend is known as an oddball in our class.

examples.ko: 혼자 여행을 다니는 저를 친구들은 별종이라고 불러요.
examples.en: My friends call me a weirdo because I travel alone.

examples.ko: 별종인 줄 알았는데 이야기해 보니 좋은 사람이에요.
examples.en: I thought he was a strange one, but after talking he's a nice person.

examples.ko: 이렇게 매운 걸 좋아하다니 정말 별종이에요.
examples.en: Liking something this spicy, you're really a strange one.

examples.ko: 별종 취급을 받아도 저는 제 방식대로 살 거예요.
examples.en: Even if I'm treated like an oddball, I'll live my own way.
There are many quirky people at my company, so it's fun.

explain: 성격이나 취향이 남과 크게 다른 사람을 가리켜요. 조금 놀리거나 낮추는 느낌이 있어서 면전에서 말하면 실례가 될 수 있어요. '괴짜'도 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.en: That person is really an oddball.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이다'를 붙여 어떤 사람이 별종이라고 말하는 기본 문장이에요. 본인 앞에서는 실례가 될 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic sentence for calling someone an oddball; it can be rude to say in front of the person.

phrases.en: My uncle is an eccentric, so he's always fun.
phrases.nuance_ko: '별종'과 비슷하지만 '괴짜'는 조금 재미있고 친근하게 말할 때도 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 별종, but 괴짜 can also sound playful and affectionate.

phrases.example: 혼자 밥을 먹는다고 별종 취급을 받았어요.
phrases.en: I was treated like a weirdo for eating alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남들이 이상한 사람처럼 대한다는 뜻으로 '취급을 받다'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 취급을 받다 to mean others treat you as odd.

explain_en: It refers to a person whose personality or taste is very different from others. It can sound a bit teasing or belittling, so saying it to someone's face may be rude. '괴짜' is used in a similar way.

examples.ko: 그 부녀는 닮은 점이 정말 많아요.
examples.en: That father and daughter have so much in common.

examples.ko: 부녀가 함께 산에 올라가는 모습이 보기 좋았어요.
examples.en: It was lovely to see the father and daughter climbing the mountain together.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 부녀의 이야기를 따뜻하게 그려요.
examples.en: This movie warmly portrays the story of a father and daughter.

examples.ko: 옆집 부녀가 매일 아침 같이 산책해요.
examples.en: The father and daughter next door walk together every morning.

examples.ko: 뉴스에 나온 부녀는 마라톤을 함께 완주했대요.
examples.en: The father and daughter on the news finished a marathon together.

examples.ko: 부녀 사이는 어릴 때와 달리 어색해졌어요.
examples.en: The relationship between father and daughter has become awkward, unlike when she was little.

explain: '부녀'는 아버지와 딸 두 사람을 한꺼번에 가리켜요. 아버지와 아들은 '부자', 어머니와 딸은 '모녀', 어머니와 아들은 '모자'라고 해요. 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 쓰고, 말할 때는 '아빠랑 딸'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 저 아빠랑 딸은 같이 자전거를 타요.
phrases.en: That father and daughter ride bikes together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 '부녀' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier phrase people use in speech instead of 부녀.

phrases.example: 두 사람은 부녀 사이라서 목소리도 닮았어요.
phrases.en: The two are father and daughter, so even their voices are alike.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아버지와 딸의 관계를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the relationship of father and daughter.

phrases.en: The sight of a father and daughter cooking together was impressive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 사람이 같이 무엇을 하는지 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say what the two do together.

explain_en: 부녀 refers to a father and his daughter together. Father and son is 부자, mother and daughter is 모녀, and mother and son is 모자. It appears mostly in writing and news; in speech people say 아빠랑 딸.

examples.ko: 그 드라마는 세 사람의 삼각관계가 중심이에요.
examples.en: That drama centers on a love triangle among three people.

examples.ko: 친구와 같은 사람을 좋아해서 삼각관계가 됐어요.
examples.en: My friend and I like the same person, so it turned into a love triangle.

examples.ko: 삼각관계 때문에 두 사람 사이가 멀어졌어요.
examples.en: The love triangle drove the two of them apart.

examples.ko: 영화 속 삼각관계가 너무 뻔해서 재미없었어요.
examples.en: The love triangle in the movie was so predictable that it wasn't fun.

examples.ko: 저는 삼각관계에 얽히는 건 정말 싫어요.
examples.en: I really hate getting caught up in a love triangle.

examples.ko: 세 나라의 삼각관계가 뉴스에 자주 나와요.
examples.en: The three-way relationship among the three countries often appears in the news.

explain: 주로 세 사람 사이의 연애 갈등을 말해서 드라마나 영화에 자주 나와요. 연애뿐 아니라 세 나라나 세 회사처럼 서로 얽힌 세 쪽의 관계에도 써요.

phrases.en: The main character gets caught in a love triangle with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세 사람 사이의 연애 갈등에 얽힐 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone gets tangled in a three-way romantic conflict.
phrases.en_equiv: to get caught in a love triangle

phrases.en: This movie deals with a complicated love triangle.
phrases.nuance_ko: 관계가 꼬여 있다는 느낌을 더할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds the feeling that the relationships are tangled.

phrases.example: 저는 삼각관계 이야기가 나오는 드라마를 좋아해요.
phrases.en: I like dramas with love triangle stories.
phrases.nuance_ko: 드라마나 소설의 내용을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when describing the plot of dramas or novels.

explain_en: It mostly refers to romantic tension among three people, a common topic in dramas and movies. It also covers any three-way relationship, such as among three countries or companies.

examples.ko: 두 분은 슬하에 딸 둘을 두고 계세요.
examples.en: They have two daughters.

examples.ko: 그 부부는 슬하에 자녀가 셋 있어요.
examples.en: That couple has three children.

examples.ko: 할아버지 슬하에서 자란 덕분에 옛이야기를 많이 알아요.
examples.en: Because I grew up in my grandfather's care, I know a lot of old stories.

examples.ko: 부모님 슬하를 떠나 처음으로 혼자 살게 됐어요.
examples.en: I left my parents' care and started living alone for the first time.
I heard the teacher has only one son.

examples.ko: 그분은 슬하에 자식이 없어서 조카를 아꼈어요.
examples.en: They had no children of their own, so they doted on their nephew.

explain: '슬하에 자녀를 두다/있다'처럼 한 덩어리로 많이 써요. 다른 사람의 가족을 소개하거나 글에서 쓰는 격식 있는 말이고, 일상 대화에서는 '아이가 둘이에요'처럼 말해요. 부모의 보호 아래라는 뜻으로 '부모님 슬하에서'도 써요.

phrases.example: 그분은 슬하에 아들 하나를 두고 계세요.
phrases.en: He has one son.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람의 자녀 수를 격식 있게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to state how many children someone else has.

phrases.en: That couple has no children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자녀가 없다는 말을 조심스럽고 격식 있게 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A careful, formal way to say someone has no children.

phrases.en: I grew up happily under my parents' care.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부모의 보호 아래서 컸다는 뜻이라 글이나 격식 있는 말에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means growing up under parents' protection, suited to writing or formal speech.

explain_en: It is mostly used as a set phrase like '슬하에 자녀를 두다/있다'. It is a formal word for introducing someone else's family or for writing; in daily talk people say '아이가 둘이에요'. It also appears as '부모님 슬하에서', meaning under a parent's care.

en: to be untrustworthy; to be insincere; to be unreliable

examples.ko: 그는 실없는 농담으로 분위기를 풀어 줬어요.
examples.en: He eased the mood with a silly joke.

examples.ko: 말이 너무 실없어서 아무도 진지하게 안 들었어요.
examples.en: His talk was so frivolous that nobody took it seriously.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 가끔 실없어 보여도 속은 깊어요.
examples.en: That person sometimes seems flippant, but he is deep inside.

examples.ko: 실없을 때가 많지만 정이 많은 친구예요.
examples.en: He is often silly, but he's a warm-hearted friend.
Why are you being so silly today?

examples.ko: 실없다고 놀림을 받아도 그는 개의치 않았어요.
examples.en: Even when teased for being flippant, he didn't mind.

explain: 농담이나 말, 웃음이 가볍고 진지하지 않을 때 쓰고, 보통 '실없는 소리/농담/웃음'처럼 붙여서 말해요. 칭찬은 아니라서 상대에게 직접 말하면 기분이 나쁠 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 실없는 소리 그만하고 일 좀 해요.
phrases.en: Stop the silly talk and get some work done.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가볍고 쓸데없는 말을 가리키는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for light and pointless talk.

phrases.example: 그는 대답 대신 실없는 웃음만 지었어요.
phrases.en: Instead of answering, he just gave a frivolous smile.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진지하지 않고 가벼운 웃음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a light, unserious smile.

phrases.example: 그렇게 자꾸 웃으면 좀 실없어 보여요.
phrases.en: If you keep laughing like that, you look a bit frivolous.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 가벼워 보인다는 뜻으로, 상대에게 직접 말하면 무례할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone looks flighty, which can be rude to say to their face.

explain_en: It describes jokes, words or laughter that are light and not serious, and usually appears as '실없는 소리/농담/웃음'. It is not a compliment, so saying it directly to someone may upset them.

examples.ko: 아이들이 말을 안 들어서 속을 썩여요.
examples.en: The kids don't listen, so they cause me a lot of worry.

examples.ko: 제발 엄마 속 좀 그만 썩이세요.
examples.en: Please stop worrying your mom so much.

examples.ko: 부모님 속을 썩인 일이 지금도 마음에 걸려요.
examples.en: I still feel bad about the times I troubled my parents.

examples.ko: 학생 때 선생님 속을 많이 썩였어요.
examples.en: When I was a student, I gave my teachers a lot of trouble.

examples.ko: 자꾸 속을 썩이면 친구들도 떠나갈 거예요.
examples.en: If you keep causing trouble, even your friends will leave.

examples.ko: 우리 강아지는 아직도 말썽을 피워서 속을 썩이는 중이에요.
examples.en: Our puppy is still causing mischief and giving me a hard time.

explain: 거의 '속을 썩이다' 모양으로 쓰고, 말썽이나 걱정거리 때문에 다른 사람을 힘들게 한다는 느낌이에요. 힘든 사람이 주어이면 '속이 썩다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 동생이 자꾸 말썽을 부려서 부모님 속을 썩여요.
phrases.en: cause someone grief
phrases.nuance_ko: 음식이 썩는다는 뜻과 관계없이, 누군가를 마음고생하게 만든다는 관용 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An idiom meaning to cause someone mental distress, unrelated to food rotting.

phrases.en: be worried sick
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정과 마음고생이 너무 커서 속이 상한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Worry and distress are so great that one is sick at heart.

explain_en: It almost always appears as '속을 썩이다' and means causing someone worry or trouble through bad behavior. When the suffering person is the subject, say '속이 썩다' instead.

en: to be idiotic; to be dumb; to be foolish

examples.ko: 그 사람은 좀 어벙해 보여도 일은 잘해요.
examples.en: He may look a bit dopey, but he does his job well.

examples.ko: 어벙한 표정으로 서 있지 말고 도와줘요.
examples.en: Don't just stand there looking blank; help me.

examples.ko: 내 동생은 어벙해서 자주 물건을 잃어버려요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is a bit spacey and often loses things.
I acted spacey and made a mistake.
The friend who seemed goofy at first is now a team leader.
Why are you so out of it today?

explain: 조금 모자라거나 멍해 보이는 사람이나 행동을 편하게 말할 때 써요. 놀리는 느낌이 있어서 윗사람이나 처음 만난 사람에게는 쓰지 않는 게 좋아요.

phrases.en: That child looked a bit dopey at first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 모자라거나 멍해 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone looks a little slow or dazed on the surface.

phrases.en: He looked at me with a blank, dopey expression.
phrases.nuance_ko: '어벙하다'를 명사 앞에 붙인 꼴로, 멍한 얼굴을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun, describing a blank face.

phrases.en: My brother isn't dopey. He is thoughtful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉보기와 달리 모자라지 않다고 부정할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to deny that someone is foolish, despite appearances.

explain_en: It is a casual word for someone or something that seems a bit dim or spaced out. It has a teasing tone, so avoid using it about people older than you or people you've just met.

examples.en: The child acts spoiled with its mother.
The youngest acts very spoiled in front of Dad.

examples.ko: 그만 응석 부리고 혼자 해 보세요.
examples.en: Stop acting spoiled and try doing it on your own.
My younger sibling is both clingy and teary.

examples.ko: 응석만 부리지 말고 스스로 해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't just act spoiled, try doing it by yourself.

examples.ko: 아이의 응석은 다 받아 주면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't give in to all of a child's whining.

explain: 보통 '응석을 부리다', '응석을 받아 주다'처럼 짝으로 써요. '어리광'과 비슷하지만, 어른이 응석을 부리면 철이 없다는 느낌이 들 수 있어요. 가까운 사람에게 기대고 싶어서 하는 행동이에요.

phrases.en: My younger sibling acts spoiled with Mom.
phrases.nuance_ko: '응석'과 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb most often paired with '응석'.

phrases.example: 할머니는 손주의 응석을 다 받아 주세요.
phrases.en: Grandma gives in to all of her grandchild's whims.
phrases.nuance_ko: 응석을 부리는 사람을 너그럽게 대해 준다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means tolerating and indulging someone who acts spoiled.

phrases.example: 동생이 태어난 뒤로 첫째의 응석이 늘었어요.
phrases.en: Since the baby was born, the eldest's clinginess has grown.
phrases.nuance_ko: 응석 부리는 일이 점점 많아질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when acting spoiled becomes more frequent.

explain_en: It is usually used in pairs like '응석을 부리다' (act spoiled) and '응석을 받아 주다' (indulge someone). It is close to '어리광', but when an adult does it, it can sound immature. It is behavior from wanting to lean on someone close.

en: to depend on; to rely on

examples.en: The child depends too much on his parents.

examples.ko: 저는 지도 앱에 의존해서 길을 찾아요.
examples.en: I rely on a map app to find my way.
This shop depends on tourists.
I want to live without relying on others.
I want to fix my habit of depending on my smartphone.

examples.ko: 우리나라는 에너지를 수입에 의존할 수밖에 없어요.
examples.en: Our country has no choice but to rely on imports for energy.

explain: 사람에게는 '에게', 사물이나 나라에는 '에'를 붙여 '~에게/에 의존하다'로 써요. '의지하다'는 마음으로 기대는 따뜻한 느낌이고, '의존하다'는 지나치게 기댄다는 느낌이 들 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 친구에게 너무 의존해서 혼자 못 해요.
phrases.en: I rely on my friend too much, so I can't do it alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이유나 방법을 이어서 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form for giving a reason or a means.

phrases.en: I don't depend on my parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 해결한다는 뜻을 나타내는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, showing that you handle things yourself.

phrases.en: When it's hard, I lean on my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의존하다'보다 마음으로 기대는 따뜻한 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Warmer than 의존하다, with the feeling of leaning on someone emotionally.

explain_en: Attach 에게 for people and 에 for things or countries: '~에게/에 의존하다'. 의지하다 has a warm feeling of leaning on someone emotionally, while 의존하다 can suggest leaning too much.

examples.ko: 그는 부탁을 하려고 나를 한참 추켜세웠어요.
examples.en: He flattered me for quite a while to ask a favor.
If you praise me too much, it actually feels like pressure.
If you build a child up with praise, they gain confidence.
It was cold, so I walked with my collar turned up.
The teacher raised their eyebrows as if surprised.

examples.ko: 사장님은 일부러 직원들을 추켜세우며 일을 시켰어요.
examples.en: The boss deliberately flattered the employees while giving them work.

explain: 옷깃이나 눈썹을 위로 올리는 뜻 외에, 사람을 지나치게 칭찬해 띄워 줄 때 많이 써요. '칭찬하다'는 중립적이지만 '추켜세우다'는 과하거나 겉치레, 때로는 속셈이 있는 칭찬 느낌이에요. '치켜세우다'도 같은 뜻으로 쓰여요.

phrases.en: His friends praise him so much that he feels uncomfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: '추켜세우다'와 같은 뜻이라서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 추켜세우다, so the two can be used interchangeably.

phrases.en: He raised his eyebrows in surprise.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 대신 몸의 일부를 위로 올린다는 원래 뜻으로 쓴 예예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the original meaning of lifting a body part upward.

phrases.en: Please don't flatter me so much. I'm embarrassed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과한 칭찬을 부드럽게 말리고 싶을 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A gentle way to ask someone to stop over-the-top praise.

explain_en: Besides lifting a collar or eyebrows upward, it is often used for praising someone excessively and building them up. '칭찬하다' is neutral, but '추켜세우다' feels over-the-top, superficial, or sometimes done with a hidden motive. '치켜세우다' is used with the same meaning.

examples.en: She raised someone else's child like her own.
Whether biological or adopted, they are all precious family.
My grandmother cherishes her daughter-in-law like her own child.
He isn't my own child, but we've grown very close.
They say there are secrets that are hard to tell even your own child.
Thank you for treating me as well as your own child.

explain: 직접 낳은 자식을 말해요. 남을 아주 가깝게 대할 때 '친자식처럼'이라는 비유로도 많이 써요. 새 배우자의 자식은 '의붓자식'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: My grandmother cared for me like her own child.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 가깝게 대한다는 비유로 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as a metaphor for treating someone very close.

phrases.en: That student is like my own child to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음이 가까운 사람에게 느끼는 정을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Expresses affection for someone you feel close to.

phrases.en: That child is not their biological child but an adopted one.
phrases.nuance_ko: 혈연 관계를 구분해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to distinguish blood relationships.

explain_en: It means a child you gave birth to yourself. It is also often used figuratively as '친자식처럼' (like one's own child) for treating others very warmly. A new spouse's child is called '의붓자식'.

examples.ko: 엄마가 아이 등을 토닥토닥 두드려 줬어요.
examples.en: Mom gently patted the child's back.
Saying 'It's okay,' I gave her shoulder gentle pats.
The baby drifted off to sleep to the sound of soft patting.

examples.ko: 토닥토닥 위로해 주는 친구가 있어서 힘이 나요.
examples.en: I have a friend who comforts me with gentle pats, and it gives me strength.
I gave the puppy's head gentle pats.
Raindrops are tapping lightly against the window.

explain: 가볍고 다정하게 두드리는 모습이나 소리를 말해요. 위로하는 장면에 잘 어울려서, 메신저에서 위로하는 마음을 '토닥토닥'이라고 쓰기도 해요. 빗방울이 약하게 떨어지는 소리에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I soothed the crying baby with gentle pats.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우는 사람을 달랠 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for comforting someone who is crying.

phrases.en: My friend gave my shoulder a comforting pat.
phrases.nuance_ko: '토닥토닥'에서 나온 동사로, 위로하는 몸짓을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb from 토닥토닥 that describes a comforting gesture.

phrases.en: I sent a message saying, 'Cheer up, there there.'
phrases.nuance_ko: 메신저에서 위로하는 마음을 짧게 보낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A short way to send comfort in a messenger chat.

explain_en: It describes the look or sound of light, tender patting. It suits comforting scenes, and people even type '토닥토닥' in chats to show comfort. It can also describe the sound of light raindrops.

examples.ko: 신입 사원은 아직 햇병아리라서 실수가 많아요.
examples.en: The new employee is still a rookie, so he makes many mistakes.
When it comes to cooking, I'm a complete beginner.
When I was a rookie, my seniors helped me a lot.
I went to the countryside to see the newly hatched chicks at the farm.
Thank you for giving a rookie like me a chance.
He's a rookie reporter, but his questions are sharp.

explain: 원래는 막 깬 병아리인데, 사람에게 쓰면 경험이 거의 없는 초보를 가리켜요. 스스로 낮춰 말할 때는 겸손하게 들리지만, 남에게 쓰면 얕보는 느낌이 날 수 있어요. 비슷한 말은 '초보', '신참'이에요.

phrases.en: I'm still a beginner at driving.
phrases.nuance_ko: '햇병아리'보다 평범하고 부드러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A plainer, softer word than 햇병아리.

phrases.en: I'm new here, so I'm still clumsy at the work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새로 들어온 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone who has newly joined.

phrases.en: I'm a green newbie, so there is a lot I don't know.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로를 낮추어 겸손하게 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits when humbly describing yourself.

explain_en: It originally means a freshly hatched chick, but for people it points to a beginner with almost no experience. Used about yourself it sounds humble, but about someone else it can sound belittling. Similar words are '초보' and '신참'.

en: to sacrifice oneself; to give up something for others

examples.ko: 부모님은 우리를 위해 많은 것을 희생하셨어요.
examples.en: My parents sacrificed a lot for us.

examples.ko: 가족을 위해 시간을 희생해야 할 때도 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes you have to give up your time for your family.
Don't work at the cost of your health.

examples.ko: 친구를 구하려고 자신을 희생한 사람 이야기를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read about a person who sacrificed himself to save a friend.

examples.ko: 저는 꿈을 위해 잠을 희생하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm sacrificing sleep for my dream.
A heart that sacrifices for everyone is remarkable.

explain: '~을 위해 ~을 희생하다'처럼 포기하는 것과 위하는 대상을 같이 말해요. 자기가 선택해서 내놓는다는 점이 '희생되다'와 달라요. 부모님, 가족 이야기에 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: I don't want to sacrifice my health.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무엇을 포기하고 싶지 않은지 '을/를'로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '을/를' to say what you don't want to give up.

phrases.en: That firefighter has a strong spirit of self-sacrifice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남을 위해 자신을 내놓는 마음을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the willingness to give up something for others.

phrases.example: 가족을 위해 희생하는 부모님께 늘 감사해요.
phrases.en: I'm always grateful to my parents, who sacrifice for the family.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람 앞에서 꾸며 주어 어떤 사람인지 설명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifies a noun to describe someone who sacrifices.

explain_en: Say what is given up and who it is for, as in '~을 위해 ~을 희생하다'. Unlike '희생되다', the person chooses to give it up. It suits talk about parents and family.

dis.h: willingly give yourself up for others
